title: Quantifying % Cover with ImageJ in Grazing Experiment Studies
author: Clara Maria Arboleda-Baena

steps.title: Capture Rock Images
steps.instruction: Capture three photographs of each rock with a ruler positioned alongside for scale: before biofilm colonization (R), after biofilm colonization (B), and after the grazing experiment (G).

steps.title: Set Image Scale and Crop
steps.instruction: Prepare each image (R, B, and G) in ImageJ to establish scale and isolate the rock.

substeps.instruction: Use the 'Straight' tool to mark 1 cm on the ruler in the photograph.
Navigate to 'Analyze > Set Scale', set 'known distance' to 1 and 'Unit of length' to cm, then click 'Ok'.
Use the 'Rectangle' tool to draw a rectangle around the perimeter of the rock.
Select 'Image > Crop' to remove the background, ensuring the rock is perfectly vertical and aligned across the R, B, and G images.

steps.title: Standardize Image Size and Save
steps.instruction: Normalize the image dimensions and save the files.

substeps.instruction: Save the photograph as a '.tif' file using the naming convention: 'Species Treatment + replicate number' + picture specification (R, B, or G).

steps.title: Process Images for Analysis
steps.instruction: Convert and threshold the .tif images for a single rock (R, B, and G) to isolate the biofilm.

substeps.instruction: Convert each picture to 8-bit format via 'Image > Type > 8-bit'.
Select the 'Red' channel and the 'Default' option.
Use the red color to define the biofilm or the darkest point on the rock.

steps.title: Quantify Area and Extract Data
steps.instruction: Analyze the particles to determine the area of the biofilm.

substeps.instruction: Set parameters: Size (cm^2) 0 - infinity; Circularity 0.00 - 1.00; Show: Nothing.
Copy the results into a table with columns for R, B, and G.

steps.title: Calculate Grazing Percentage
steps.instruction: Determine the grazing percentage using the values obtained from the three images.

substeps.instruction: Subtract the biofilm picture value (B) from the grazing picture value (G).
Subtract the background value obtained from the rock picture (R) from the previous result.
